definition: Conscious memory is memory that a person can knowingly recall, such as correctly remembering a previous choice or rejection. In this source, it refers to explicit awareness of past choices and is linked to episodic memory.

reasons: The packet supports that “conscious memory of previous choices” is necessary for the effect, operationalized as items being “correctly remembered as chosen or rejected” (choice stage).

The definition’s claim that, “in this source, it refers to explicit awareness of past choices,” is not explicitly stated in the packet; the packet describes correct remembering but does not define conscious memory as explicit awareness.

The definition’s claim that this is “linked to episodic memory” is not supported beyond a general statement that relations with episodic memory “remain strongly debated”; the packet does not state a specific linkage between conscious memory and episodic memory as a meaning of the term.

The source supports conscious memory of previous choices and correct remembering of chosen or rejected items, but it does not support the added claim that this sense is linked to episodic memory; the article says that relation remains strongly debated.
